module_title: Advanced Analysis - Geomorphology, Submergence, and Strategic Islands
introduction: This advanced level explores the geological structure of the coasts (submergent vs. emergent), the Arakan Yoma origin theory for the Andamans, and other critical strategic islands of India.

core_concepts.title: Submergent vs. Emergent Coasts
core_concepts.description: The West Coast is a 'Submergent' (drowned) coast. Because the water is deep right near the land, it provides ideal conditions for 'Natural Harbors' (like Mumbai, Marmagao, Kochi). The East Coast is an 'Emergent' (uplifted) coast, making the waters shallow, hence it has more 'Artificial Ports' (like Chennai).

core_concepts.title: Origin of Andamans (Arakan Yoma Extension)
core_concepts.description: Geologically, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are considered a southward oceanic extension of the 'Arakan Yoma' mountain range of Myanmar. The mountains submerged under the sea, and only their highest peaks are visible as islands.

core_concepts.title: Duncan Passage
core_concepts.description: It is a strait that separates 'South Andaman' from 'Little Andaman'. (Note: The capital city, Port Blair, is located in South Andaman).

core_concepts.title: Other Important Strategic Islands
core_concepts.description: 1. Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh): Located near Pulicat Lake, it houses ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre. 2. Abdul Kalam Island / Wheeler Island (Odisha): Used by DRDO for missile testing. 3. New Moore Island: A newly emerged island in the Ganga delta, once disputed between India and Bangladesh.

important_entities.name: Pamban Island
important_entities.significance: Located in the Gulf of Mannar between India (Tamil Nadu) and Sri Lanka. It forms a part of 'Adam's Bridge' (Ram Setu).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In UPSC exams, just knowing 'Andaman' isn't enough. They will ask exactly where Port Blair is located: North, Middle, South, or Little Andaman? The correct answer is 'South Andaman'.
Eastern rivers form deltas because the emergent coast is shallow, giving sediments room to fan out. The western coast is submergent and deep, so rivers dump directly into the sea, forming estuaries.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: West is Deep (Submerged), East is Shallow (Emergent)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Deep = Natural Ports + Estuaries. Shallow = Deltas + Artificial Ports.

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, firmly connect the 'submergent' nature of the western coast to the development of natural harbors.
Be very clear on the different functions of Sriharikota (ISRO space launches) vs. Wheeler Island/Abdul Kalam Island (DRDO missile testing). They are frequently swapped in trap questions.
